description: Generate a new build token for a site and put it where the build reads it. By default the token is written straight into the .env file (TUSK_SITE, TUSK_URL, TUSK_TOKEN; existing lines replaced, the rest kept, .env added to .gitignore if it is not ignored) and only a masked preview comes back, so the secret never enters your context. Set the same TUSK_TOKEN on the host by reading it from .env without printing it (e.g. grep ^TUSK_TOKEN= .env | cut -d= -f2- piped into the host CLI). Pass reveal:true ONLY if you genuinely must handle the value yourself. This is the token the build scripts (tusk-pull.mjs) use to fetch the published snapshot; it is NOT the access token this MCP authenticates with. Rotating invalidates the previous build token: update the host after rotating, or the dashboard will show "Build token out of date".

envPath.description: Env file to write, default ".env" in the current directory.

reveal.description: Return the plaintext instead of writing .env. Default false.

name: rotate_build_token
title: Rotate build token
